cells.tense: The wide view is here now, and the shared joy keeps feeding it.
cells.ask: Name one thing that makes sense across the whole of this, then say it out loud where someone who was there can hear it.
cells.core: You can stand inside what's happening and still catch the shape of it. That's the hard part and you're doing it. The celebrating in the room is not noise around the view. It's one way the pieces show themselves. When people let go together and nobody is performing, the meaning gets shared plainly, and you can read what's actually common here rather than what should be. You see the whole shape, you say what you see, and the room stays warm while you do it. The pattern and the pleasure are the same motion right now. You're not above the party and you're not lost in it.

cells.verb: celebrate the shared meaning until it shows the whole pattern
cells.place: inside the pattern, reading it while still in the room

cells.tense: You're reading the celebration before it happens, bracing for a pattern nobody has made yet.
cells.ask: Leave one gathering you'd normally organize entirely alone this week, and watch what the room does without your hand on it.
cells.core: The group hasn't said a word yet and you've already mapped how it will go — who will click, where the mood turns, what it will all mean. So you steer the joy toward the meaning you've assigned it. The room ends up feeling handled rather than shared. The clean version is simpler: you catch the shape while you're in it, not ahead of it, and that adds to the moment instead of managing it. Right now you're right about a lot and present for less. Letting the meaning get built in the room, at room speed, is the way back. You'll know less in advance and have more to keep.

cells.tense: You stepped off to the side a while back, and the shared joy has been happening at a distance since.
cells.ask: Ask one person to walk you through something they made, and follow the shape they point at until you can say it back to them.
cells.core: You got pulled out of the shared moment and stayed out. There was a room where laughing together landed wrong, or where what moved you didn't get said, and you've been watching from the edge since. Watching from the edge is a real skill — you can read a structure from outside it, and that has uses. What it can't do is read a room you're not in. The working version has you inside the thing, the pattern arriving through being part of it rather than instead of it. The celebration keeps trying to hand you the whole from the inside. You've been taking notes on it and skipping the part where you're there. Warmth comes back first; the wide view follows from inside it.
cells.sheetLine: You learned to watch the room instead of being in it.

cells.tense: The pattern is being made sense of, and you talk as if the room did the seeing.
cells.ask: Call one gathered moment yours out loud to the people who were there, and leave the word us out of the sentence.
cells.core: In the middle of a group you're the one quietly tracking what is happening and what it adds up to, and people lean on it. You say the room has that quality, or that it's obvious, or that anyone would notice. What that leaves out is you. The reading is happening and the reading is yours — it's already your work. Done plainly, you know you're the one holding it, and you can say so without making it a production. Tonight the sight is running and your name isn't on it. Say it plainly once and the room gets a person to thank instead of an atmosphere to enjoy. That's smaller and truer than it sounds.
